gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each kit costs per 4K60 screen. Including the HDMI loop-out every kit has, the OREI UHD12-EX115-K comes to $46.66 per screen ($139.99 / 3 screens), the J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE to $60.50 ($302.49 / 5) and the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K to $85.80 ($429 / 5). The two cheaper 1x4 kits (J-Tech 14EX60-AE and OREI UHD14-EX115-K) were both sold out at their makers' stores on 2026-11-13.
standout_why: I compared against the OREI support articles ChatGPT cited (UHD12-EX115-K, UHD14-EXB400-K) and the top result (UHD14-EX115-K). They list 4K60 and 1080p reach, the loop-out, PoC and power draw, but they give no price. So none of them gives a cost per screen, a cost per foot of 4K60 reach, power per receiver or stock status. ChatGPT's answer gave whole-kit prices only, and its '4 TVs, value' card ($302.49 J-Tech) is sold out at J-Tech.
decides: This confirms the OREI UHD12-EX115-K as the cheapest way to put 4K60 on more than one screen: $46.66 per screen if you count the loop-out, $70.00 per remote screen if you don't. For 4 remote TVs it changes the pick. ChatGPT's value pick (J-Tech, $75.62 per remote screen) and OREI's cheaper UHD14-EX115-K ($62.50 per remote screen) are both out of stock at their makers. That leaves the in-stock UHD14-EXB400-K at $107.25 per remote screen. It also has the lowest cost per foot of 4K60 reach ($1.09/ft over 394 ft), but it draws 8.75 W per receiver against 4.14 W for the UHD12-EX115-K.
